analytical_question: As of 2026-10-13, America/New_York, should this hypothetical delivery fleet undertake a grid-export charging pilot while protecting daily route readiness?
general_et_finding: V2G requires capable vehicles and charging equipment plus utility authorization for reverse power flow; V2B backup does not establish grid-export readiness. The supplied evidence establishes prerequisites, not fleet-wide maturity, diffusion, or commercial viability. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
application_finding: For this application, technical feasibility is insufficient: export must preserve the energy needed for scheduled routes. A non-export proof of concept can test reserve controls, but cannot demonstrate operational grid-export performance or economic value.
organization_specific_finding: Hypothetical assumptions establish written pilot permission, supplier-confirmed compatibility, and engineering isolation capability. These support preparation, but unverified battery-warranty and commercial terms leave consequential exposure unresolved; innovator appetite does not imply acceptance of that exposure.

evidence.claim: DOE distinguishes V2B from V2G and identifies capable equipment and utility interconnection permission as relevant prerequisites.
evidence.source_or_reference: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging — U.S. Department of Energy, Managed and Bidirectional Charging. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Supplied packet retrieved 2026-10-13; page publication date unstated.
evidence.evidence_type: Authoritative general guidance; supplied dated evidence packet.
evidence.notes: The undated live page corroborates the packet's stated scope; its historical version was not independently verified. No later developments are used, and this guidance establishes no fleet-specific permission, warranty, or savings.

evidence.claim: Permission, compatibility confirmation, and trial-isolation capability are assumed; commercial terms and battery warranty remain unverified.
evidence.evidence_type: Hypothetical input assumptions, not externally verified organizational evidence.
evidence.notes: Supplier confirmation is a case assumption, not independent technical validation. These inputs are not field-deployment evidence.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Counter-case: assumed permission, compatibility, and isolation capability favor a bounded export experiment once warranty exposure and pilot obligations are explicitly resolved.
Neither route-reserve control performance nor export economics has been demonstrated for this fleet.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Confidence is high that unresolved warranty and contractual exposure justify deferring export under these assumptions. Confidence is low about eventual profitability and delivery reliability because neither has case-specific operating evidence.
value_opportunity_implication: The proposed value is learning whether parked vehicles can provide grid services without disrupting deliveries, not proven savings. Treat ordinary managed charging as the strongest non-export alternative and compare incremental export value against it.
risk_governance_implication: Before export, obtain applicable warranty terms and explicit allocation of battery, equipment, and delivery-loss exposure. Proposed pilot safeguards should include a protected route-energy reserve, human stop authority, and a tested return to non-export charging.
recommendation_management_implication: Defer operational grid export: unresolved warranty and contractual exposure are decisive. Immediately pursue terms clarification and a non-export reserve-control proof of concept; export remains blocked. Pass operating capacity and implementation ownership assessment to the Organizational Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reconsider as a bounded experiment when written warranty applicability and pilot terms resolve liability exposure, and non-export testing demonstrates reserve protection and shutdown behavior.
If subsequent testing cannot preserve route readiness, reject this application for the present regardless of innovation appetite.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Obtain vehicle-specific battery-warranty provisions and pilot contracts covering compensation, discharge obligations, penalties, and liability before authorizing export.
Obtain route-energy requirements and non-export control-test results; abstain from claiming profitability, delivery reliability, or readiness for routine adoption.
